subject.title: feat: clarify publisher state and discovery labels

question: Should ClawHub expose `claimState`, `officialState`, and `restrictionState` as a supported official-publisher admin API contract once the inactive-member false positive is fixed and runtime proof is supplied?
rationale: The patch introduces durable identity and trust vocabulary that downstream clients can depend on; deciding whether that contract belongs in the supported API requires maintainer intent beyond a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Fix, prove, then accept the contract
options.body: Require observed-active-user derivation and redacted live API proof, then review the vocabulary as the proposed supported admin contract.

options.title: Land a spec-only slice
options.body: Keep the internal state-boundary documentation but remove the new runtime response field until a sponsored API design is ready.

options.title: Defer the vocabulary
options.body: Leave the existing official-publisher API unchanged until broader claim and verification policy is explicitly established.

recommendation.title: Fix, prove, then accept the contract
recommendation.body: Require observed-active-user derivation and redacted live API proof, then review the vocabulary as the proposed supported admin contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the strongest current-main owner signal for the official-publisher administration and client-schema surfaces changed by this PR.
